subject.title: [Feature]: bearer token authentication for proxy servers

question: Should OpenClaw add first-party mobile proxy-auth credentials to setup codes/manual Gateway settings, and if so which credential types are approved for the first secure slice?
rationale: The request changes pre-Gateway authentication, mobile secret storage, WebSocket upgrade headers, and possibly browser/OIDC redirect handling, so code inspection cannot safely choose the permanent credential lifecycle or trust boundary without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Approve scoped static-header slice
options.body: Implement Basic/bearer/fixed-header/cookie support with TLS-only sending, explicit storage/clearing/redaction rules, Android/iOS parity, and defer OIDC to a separate design.

options.title: Design full OIDC proxy auth first
options.body: Pause static header work until maintainers define browser-return, token exchange, app-link, and credential lifecycle boundaries for identity-provider proxy auth.

options.title: Decline mobile proxy credentials
options.body: Keep mobile clients limited to direct/tailnet/trusted Gateway auth paths and document authenticated reverse proxies as unsupported for native apps.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped static-header slice
recommendation.body: Implement Basic/bearer/fixed-header/cookie support with TLS-only sending, explicit storage/clearing/redaction rules, Android/iOS parity, and defer OIDC to a separate design.

likelyOwner.reason: The setup-code bootstrap-token and Gateway auth contract history makes this the best available owner signal for the cross-platform auth-boundary choice.
